opening.text: A porch light is a small thing. It doesn't talk. It doesn't ask for anything. It just says, “Someone is home. You are welcome here.” Ministering can be like that. We don't need big words. We just need to be a light someone can count on.

mainMessage.text: Ministering is being a steady light for one person at a time, with love as the reason.

blocks.text: **One by one** The Savior cared for people one at a time. He asks us to do the same.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “Ministering as the Savior Does” from the April 2018 general conference.
True ministering is accomplished one by one with love as the motivation.
Love is the reason.
**As He would** We ask what the Savior would do. Then we do it. Lives are waiting.
By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
As followers of Jesus Christ, we seek to minister to others as He would because lives are waiting to change.
Minister as He would.
**Becoming part of a life** A porch light is not on for one night. Ministering is not a visit. It is becoming part of someone's life.

And it came to pass that he said unto them: Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all things, and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—
Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “Ministering as the Savior Does” from the April 2018 general conference.
It looks like becoming part of someone’s life and caring about him or her.
Become part of a life.
**Everyone is a shepherd** No one is left out. Every member can watch over someone.
I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.
Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Shepherding Souls” from the October 2018 general conference.
Every man, woman, and child in the kingdom of God is a shepherd.
Everyone can watch over someone.
**Light for the whole street** One porch light helps a whole street. Inspired ministering blesses homes and wards.

I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
Inspired ministering blesses families and individuals; it also strengthens wards and branches.
The whole street is lit.
**Because He asked** We don't turn the light on for praise. We do it because the Savior asked us to.
For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:
Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Shepherding Souls” from the October 2018 general conference.
We reach out in love to others because it is what our Savior commanded us to do.
He asked us to.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone ministered to them, or when they ministered to someone else. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Four friends and the roof

blocks.text: Four men carried a sick friend to Jesus Christ. The crowd was too thick to get through. So they opened the roof and lowered him down.

And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four. And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay. When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.
The man couldn't get to the Savior alone. His friends carried him. Ministering is sometimes just that: helping someone get where they need to go.

application.text: First, think of one person you have been asked or feel prompted to care for. Second, ask yourself, “What do they need?” Third, do one small thing for them this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father knows each of us by name. I know a small act of love can reach a heavy heart. I know Jesus Christ is the Good Shepherd. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A sweater is made of one long thread. It is looped and pulled through, again and again. Alone, the thread is weak. Joined with itself, it holds. People are like that. We hold together when someone reaches out and loops a thread through our life. Ministering is how that thread is passed.

mainMessage.text: Ministering weaves a thread between lives. It turns separate people into a strong fabric.

blocks.text: **One thread at a time** A sweater is made one stitch at a time. We reach one person, then another.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “Ministering as the Savior Does” from the April 2018 general conference.
True ministering is accomplished one by one with love as the motivation.
One stitch at a time.
**The pattern we follow** The knitter follows a pattern. We follow the Savior's.
By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
As followers of Jesus Christ, we seek to minister to others as He would because lives are waiting to change.
Follow His pattern.
**Woven in** A thread isn't added at the end. It is woven in. Ministering is joining someone's life.

And it came to pass that he said unto them: Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all things, and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—
Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “Ministering as the Savior Does” from the April 2018 general conference.
It looks like becoming part of someone’s life and caring about him or her.
Be woven in.
**Everyone holds a needle** Every member can pick up the thread. No one has to be called twice.
I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.
Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Shepherding Souls” from the October 2018 general conference.
Every man, woman, and child in the kingdom of God is a shepherd.
Pick up the thread.
**A stronger fabric** As threads join, the cloth gets stronger. Ministering strengthens families, wards and branches.

I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
Inspired ministering blesses families and individuals; it also strengthens wards and branches.
The cloth grows strong.
**Woven with love** The reason matters. We weave because the Savior has asked us to, and because we care.
For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:
Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Shepherding Souls” from the October 2018 general conference.
We reach out in love to others because it is what our Savior commanded us to do.
Weave with love.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone's steady friendship made a difference. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Peter and the man at the gate

blocks.text: A man who couldn't walk begged at the temple gate. Peter had no money to give.

Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk. And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength.
Peter gave what he had. He didn't have gold. He had faith, and he took the man by the hand. We don't need to have everything. We need to give what we have.

application.text: First, list the people near you who might need a thread. Second, pick one. Third, share a short message, a visit or a kind act this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God uses us to care for each other. I know we can give what we have and it is enough. I know Jesus Christ takes each of us by the hand. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: In a relay race, no one runs the whole way. Each runner carries the baton a short distance and hands it on. The race is won because people trust each other with it. Ministering is a bit like that. We carry love for a while to the person we are given. And we keep our hand steady.

mainMessage.text: Ministering is carrying love to one person, steadily, the way a runner carries a baton.

blocks.text: **One runner, one hand** A baton goes into one hand at a time. Love reaches one person at a time too.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “Ministering as the Savior Does” from the April 2018 general conference.
True ministering is accomplished one by one with love as the motivation.
One hand at a time.
**Running His course** The runner stays in the lane. We stay on the Savior's path.
By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
As followers of Jesus Christ, we seek to minister to others as He would because lives are waiting to change.
Stay in His lane.
**Staying close** A good handoff takes two people running side by side. Ministering means staying close enough to care.

And it came to pass that he said unto them: Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all things, and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—
Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “Ministering as the Savior Does” from the April 2018 general conference.
It looks like becoming part of someone’s life and caring about him or her.
Run beside them.
**Every runner on the team** No one sits out. Every member has a leg to run.
I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.
Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Shepherding Souls” from the October 2018 general conference.
Every man, woman, and child in the kingdom of God is a shepherd.
Everyone has a leg to run.
**The whole team wins** When each runner does their part, the whole team crosses the line. Ministering blesses homes and wards.

I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
Inspired ministering blesses families and individuals; it also strengthens wards and branches.
The team wins together.
**Why we run** We don't run for a medal. We run because the Savior asked us to.
For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:
Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Shepherding Souls” from the October 2018 general conference.

He asked us to run.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone showed up for them in a hard moment. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Job's friends come

blocks.text: Job lost nearly everything. When his friends heard, they didn't wait to be asked.

Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.
They made a plan to go. They traveled to be with him. Showing up is often the first and best part of ministering.

application.text: First, think of someone going through a hard time. Second, decide how you will show up: a visit, a call or a meal. Third, set a day and keep it.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Jesus Christ never stops carrying us. I know when we show up for each other, hearts are lifted. I know Heavenly Father hears us when we ask how to help. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A bridge doesn't ask what is in the river. It just connects one side to the other. People standing on opposite banks can finally meet. Ministering is a bridge. It joins one life to another and says, “You don't have to cross alone.”

mainMessage.text: Ministering builds a bridge from one heart to another, one plank at a time.

blocks.text: **One plank at a time** A bridge is built slowly. We start with one person and one small act.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “Ministering as the Savior Does” from the April 2018 general conference.
True ministering is accomplished one by one with love as the motivation.
Start with one plank.
**The Builder's plan** Every good bridge follows a plan. Ours is the Savior's.
By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
As followers of Jesus Christ, we seek to minister to others as He would because lives are waiting to change.
Build by His plan.
**A bridge that stays** A bridge isn't taken down after one crossing. We stay. We become part of the person's life.

And it came to pass that he said unto them: Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all things, and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—
Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “Ministering as the Savior Does” from the April 2018 general conference.
It looks like becoming part of someone’s life and caring about him or her.
The bridge stays.
**Everyone can build** You don't need a title or special tools. Every member can lay a plank.
I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.
Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Shepherding Souls” from the October 2018 general conference.
Every man, woman, and child in the kingdom of God is a shepherd.
Everyone can lay a plank.
**Many cross** A bridge serves more than one traveler. Ministering strengthens families, wards and branches.

I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
Inspired ministering blesses families and individuals; it also strengthens wards and branches.
Many cross over.
**Built on love** A bridge needs a strong foundation. Ours is love, and the Savior's command.
For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:
Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Shepherding Souls” from the October 2018 general conference.
We reach out in love to others because it is what our Savior commanded us to do.
Love is the foundation.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a friendship was a bridge for them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jonathan and David

blocks.text: Jonathan was a king's son. David was a shepherd. They came from very different places.
Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
Jonathan loved David as he loved himself. He made a promise to stand by him. Real friendship crosses the gap between two lives.

application.text: First, think of someone who feels far away. Second, ask what small plank you could lay: a message, a note, a visit. Third, do it this week.

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father puts people in our path on purpose. I know love can cross any distance. I know Jesus Christ is the bridge to us all. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A good shepherd walks out at night to find one sheep. The other ninety-nine are safe. But one is missing, and that one matters. Ministering follows the same pattern. We notice who is missing, and we go.

mainMessage.text: Ministering is going after the one, the way a shepherd does, with love as the reason.

blocks.text: **The one who matters** The shepherd counts. He knows when one is gone. We notice too.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “Ministering as the Savior Does” from the April 2018 general conference.
True ministering is accomplished one by one with love as the motivation.
The one matters.
**Following the Good Shepherd** We go where He would go. We do what He would do.
By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
As followers of Jesus Christ, we seek to minister to others as He would because lives are waiting to change.
Go as He would.
**Walking with the flock** A shepherd doesn't stand far off. He walks with the sheep. We become part of the lives we care for.

Walk with them.
**All of us are shepherds** The Savior gave the work to all of us. No one is too young or too new.
I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.
Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Shepherding Souls” from the October 2018 general conference.
Every man, woman, and child in the kingdom of God is a shepherd.
We are all shepherds.
**A stronger flock** When the lost are found, the whole flock is safer. Ministering strengthens families, wards and branches.

I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Ministering” from the April 2023 general conference.
Inspired ministering blesses families and individuals; it also strengthens wards and branches.

**Because He commanded** The shepherd doesn't search for praise. He searches because he loves the sheep. We go because the Savior asked us to.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone came looking for them, or when they went looking for someone. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The lost sheep

blocks.text: Jesus Christ told of a man with a hundred sheep. One went missing.

What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
He didn't scold the sheep. He carried it home, and he was glad. That is how the Savior treats each of us. And it is how we can treat each other.

application.text: First, think of someone who has been missing from your circle or from church. Second, reach out with a kind word and no pressure. Third, keep going back, gently, until they know they are missed.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Jesus Christ is the Good Shepherd. I know He goes after each one of us. I know Heavenly Father gives us the chance to help. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
